publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Population Survey and Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, as copied by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)
title_or_table: FRED series UNRATE (Unemployment Rate) and JTSJOL (Job Openings: Total Nonfarm), downloaded together as fredgraph.csv
observation_period: Quarterly averages, first quarter of 2001 to third quarter of 2026
universe_or_base: Unemployment rate: unemployed people as a percent of the civilian labor force, 16 and over. Job openings: open positions at nonfarm employers on the last business day of the month
unit: unemployment_rate in percent and job_openings_millions in millions of openings, each the average of the quarter's three seasonally adjusted monthly values, rounded to four decimals
vintage: FRED values as of Dustin Cathcart's download on November 11, 2026 (attached to the studio chat at 22:27 UTC); SHA-256 10c1d1ed61e8b494195f087331ad53aa7651ba3ceca05597599a7953c1a58532. BLS revises recent months and seasonal factors, so later downloads can differ. The unemployment rate comes from the Bureau’s Employment Situation for October 2026, released November 6, 2026, and job openings from its Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey for September 2026, released November 3, 2026
qualification: The unemployment rate has no value for October 2025: the cell is blank in FRED's file, matching the month the Current Population Survey collected no data during the lapse in federal funding (the Census Bureau notes the same gap in its CPS/HVS tables). A line chart breaks at that month. Job openings run one month behind the unemployment rate; recent months are preliminary

unemployment_rate.description: average of the three monthly rates; empty where a month has none

job_openings_millions.description: average of the three monthly counts, in millions

printed_source_line: Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Population Survey and Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, releases for October 2026 (November 6, 2026) and September 2026 (November 3, 2026), unemployment rate and job openings, seasonally adjusted, 2001 to 2026, United States, via FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Retrieved November 11, 2026. Quarterly averages computed by Oath & Action; no unemployment rate was published for October 2025, so the fourth quarter of 2025 has no average; recent months are preliminary and will be revised.
derivation: For each calendar quarter from the first of 2001 to the third of 2026 in which job openings cover all three months, the average of the three monthly values of each series (job openings in millions); a quarter with a month that has no unemployment rate takes no unemployment average
notes: The monthly file starts job openings in December 2000; the first full quarter is the first of 2001. October 2026's unemployment rate is left out, since its quarter is not complete
